st.t: Photo Story of HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj's Empathy and Compassion, Surat - 23 December, 1999
w: A young, poor boy had met with an accident in Valsad during mid-December. He was hospitalized at the Mahavir General Hospital in Surat. A week later, when Swamishri arrived in Surat, he remembered the ailing boy. Swamishri expressed his wish to visit the boy. Immediately, all the requisite arrangements of transport and appointment to the hospital were made.

As Swamishri's car arrived, both sides of the road to the hospital were excavated for a new water line. Because of the narrow road, Swamishri's car could not go any further. Subsequently, Swamishri walked the distance of 100 to 150 meters during the late busy morning hours.
Swamishri walked along the narrow uneven footpath, between the shops and the excavated road, with the support of attendant sadhus.

Swamishri came to the thin boy's bedside in an ICU ward of the hospital. The boy's head was bandaged and IV fluids were supplied through a catheter in his arm. Swamishri gently placed his hand on the boy's head and greeted him, "Prashant, Jai Swaminarayan..." And then garlanded the boy and also placed sanctified flowers on his chest and head. Prayers were then offered for Prashant's quick recovery. Swamishri reassured Shantilal, the boy's father, not to hesitate in asking for any help required.

After coming out of the hospital, there was an excavated channel, nearly 2.5 feet wide. With the support of the attendant sadhus, Swamishri jumped across the channel and returned back to the car. Disregarding the frailties of old age, Swamishri's empathy and compassion reached out to a poor, ailing boy.
In the morning, before puja, Swamishri performed the murti pratishtha of the murtis to bge installed in the mandirs at Mohadi, Japi, Songir, Kusumbe and Galvada, all in the Khandesh region.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj's 81st birthday celebrations.

st.t: 81st Birthday Celebration of Pramukh Swami Maharaj - Birthday Celebration page-2
w: Swamishri offers prayers for peace in India and throughout the world ... inaugurates an audio cassette on Yogiji Maharaj's narration of moral stories
Pujya Kothari Swami and Pujya Tyagvallabh Swami offer a garland of candies to Swamishri Principal devotees of India, UK, USA, Canada, E.Africa, Australia, ... after greeting Swamishri

Finally, Swamishri blessed the mammoth gathering of devotees, "One's life should be pure to spread the torch kindled by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and subsequently spread by Gunatitanand Swami, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. To purify one's life one must obey the moral commands prescribed in the Shikshapatri and offer upasana to Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Upasana means to believe God to be the all-doer. If one realizes the glory of God then one shall see virtues in everyone ..."
K.R. Shreenivas, bureau chief of a prestigious English daily, came for Swamishri's darshan and blessings.
Shreenivas said, “I only want to write good things and do good things in my life.”

Swamishri was pleased by his sentiments and added, “By giving good things people find peace. Otherwise misunderstandings are created in people. Write on religious and social things so that they are inspired. No matter what type of news you get, but one must think about what and how to write it. One should not print news that create unrest and agitation in people. One must see as to how peace can be maintained.”
Shreenivas, “We want to do that.”
Swamishri reiterated again, “No mater what news you get but they should be written in such a fashion that it does not create misunderstandings and anger in the public, but maintains peace.
Shreenivas: “It is our aim to print everything positive so that everyone enjoys it.”
Swamishri: “Yes, that's right. So that there is joy in people, peace in society and country, and peace among religions.”
Shreenivas: “We print articles to inspire progress in others.”
Swamishri: “Our work is to see how our country can progress. To inspire others is our work. If there is agitation or strife then there can be no progress .”
Swamishri's message of positive reporting for peace and progress in people and country are needed in our conflicting and trouble-filled times.
At 11.00 am Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of murtis for BAPS Swaminaryan Mandirs for the villages of Betavad and Vadgam.

ds.t: It is the power of their resolve
w: Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat to feed Thakorji. Meanwhile Adarshjivan Swami said, "Sant Swami used to say that you have done ten times the work of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj."
Swamishri said, "Originally the resolves are theirs. That mandirs be built and satsang grow are their resolves, and so the work is done."
Adarshjivan Swami said, "They made the resolve, but holding on to the resolve and doing the work is no less important."
Swamishri said, "It happened because it was their resolve! There is power in their resolve! Because of that it goes on."
Adarshjivan Swami said, "There may be power in the seed, but someone is needed to water it, to give it manure and water. Only then will the tree grow!"
Swamishri said, "But only if the seed is true do the manure and water bear fruit."
Adarshjivan Swami said, "In this matter you never let anyone pin it on you. Your humility is beyond understanding."

Saying this, he continued, "This year, in just one year, you installed murtis in 18 hari mandirs. You laid the foundations of 9 hari mandirs. You installed murtis in two shikharbaddh mandirs and laid the foundations of 4 shikharbaddh mandirs. You created a new inner sanctum in Akshardham, Delhi. You completed the 'Sachchidanand Water Show' of Gandhinagar Akshardham. You completed about 40 such projects in just one year. That is, on average you accomplished three and a half projects a month. Also, you gave diksha to 22 seekers. At 89 years of age, this work could never have been possible without your effort."

Swamishri at once said, "Originally all this is the power of the resolve of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj wanted to make sadhus and had resolved that 'satsang should grow', and so everything happens."
Krishnavallabh Swami said to Adarshjivan Swami, "From him there will be only one answer."
Swamishri said, "That is what it is, isn't it! Yogibapa used to do dhun in person at the Akshar Deri that 'satsang should grow, sadhus should increase', and so it happens."
Adarshjivan Swami said, "It is a fact that there was a resolve, but turning that resolve into reality is no small thing."
Swamishri said, "The power is certainly God's, but it happened because there was power in their resolve."
Krishnavallabh Swami said, "If you had not travelled, how would all this have happened?"
Swamishri said, "Yogiji Maharaj had resolved, 'Satsang must be increased'; since he said that, we have to travel, don't we!"

Adarshjivan Swami said, "Your detachment and humility often create confusion. How can one always remain so humble and so detached? Others, if you praise them a lot, will at least once say, 'I did this.'"
Swamishri said, "For us there is only one thing. Whatever the guru has said, that is what happens. The work has been done according to his resolve. That itself is our award."

The sadhus turned it around this way and that and spoke in every way in praise of Swamishri's work, but in every reply Swamishri kept repeating that "the work has been done only because of the resolves made by the gurus", giving an ideal example of devotion to the guru.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj said to the sadhus who had come from the Dhulia hostel, "Yogibapa used to say, keep unity, friendliness and oneness. Keep everyone in harmony and of one mind. If someone speaks harshly, tolerate it. Some may feel, 'Am I a donkey?' But we are human beings. If someone speaks like that, it is the speaker's mouth that will smell. We have come to remove our own natures and faults; Maharaj will see to others. The group there is small, but because it is of one mind, the work gets done. We should do good to everyone. Yogibapa was in Atladra, and someone stole something; he was caught and taken to Yogibapa, and Yogibapa said, 'How is he a thief? He is a mukta.' What vision Yogibapa had! Wherever he looked, he saw nothing but God. If we keep such knowledge and understanding......"
